title: evening-smoke-prefill-and-kernel-tuning-jot-2029-04-11
content:
Context:
This is a short, informal capture of tonight's 'quiet-hours' smoke tests focused on prefill behavior, KV cache TTL adjustments, and a lightweight kernel scheduling tweak (coalesce threshold). Goal was to validate that the small heuristic change reduces noisy tail latency without regressing steady-state throughput. Running on staging-n1 (8xA100-equivalent) with representative QPS replay from last week's peak trace.

Summary highlights:
- Small kernel change (coalesce-threshold: 8 -> 6) produced a visible P95 latency reduction on short-seq requests during low-traffic windows. P95 dropped from ~124ms -> ~98ms for the short-crit path (sequence length <= 64).
- KV cache TTL experiments: lowering TTL from 120s -> 40s increased cache churn but improved cold-start tail for some long-running sessions; overall cache hit-rate dropped 2.6pp (from 87.3% -> 84.7%).
- Micro-batching policy: bumped target batch size for low-latency lanes from 4 -> 6; observed a modest 6% throughput increase but 3–4ms median latency bump for single-request flows when kernel coalesce disabled.

Detailed observations:
1) Kernel coalesce threshold change (experiment ID: kernel-coalesce-2029-04-11-a):
   - What we changed: lowered the early-coalesce threshold to favor forming slightly larger batches earlier in the loop for short sequences.
   - Why: hypothesis was that some single-shot short seq requests were getting paired too late, introducing jitter; earlier coalesce should smooth tail.
   - Metrics: short-seq P50 18ms -> 20ms (small increase), P95 124ms -> 98ms (large improvement), P99 256ms -> 220ms.
   - CPU/GPU impact: GPU utilization +3% during replay windows; no OOMs observed.
   - Notes: Improvement concentrated on lanes with mixed-request sizes. For pure long-seq workloads this change produced no benefit and slightly increased token latency.

2) KV cache TTL lowering (experiment ID: kvttl-smoke-0429-b):
   - Change: TTL 120s -> 40s for prefix caches in staging cluster.
   - Observed: cache hit-rate drop ~2.6 percentage points; tail token latency for new sessions improved ~8% because the system avoided serving stale/less-optimal cached entries.
   - Tradeoff: increased backend pressure (more re-computation), higher memory churn. Exported memory churn metric rose ~12% and background eviction cycles increased.
   - Action: consider a conditional TTL lowering only for sessions where cache staleness score > 0.7 (scoring heuristic is in RFC linked below).

3) Micro-batching target bump for low-latency lanes:
   - Change: target batch size 4 -> 6 (soft target; respects latency-SLO gated path).
   - Observed: throughput up ~6% on throughput-oriented traces; single-request median latency increased by ~3–4ms.
   - Observability: added metrics to per-request tags to separate effects; see linked PR for new metric names.

Incidents/Regression checks:
- No regressions on model quality observed (ran golden prompt set).
- One flaky test surfaced in the release-candidate harness: compact-kv-eviction test intermittently fails under high evictions; created SRV-4221 to investigate.

Open questions and hypotheses:
- Is a global TTL tweak worthwhile, or should we route TTL behavior by traffic cohort? (suggestion: TTL=40s only for new-session cohort with high prefix variability).
- Kernel coalesce improvement looks promising but could harm long-seq tails; need A/B by model profile.
- Could we combine a small coalesce change with a fast-path single-request bypass to preserve medians?

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Miguel: spin an A/B on prod-like cluster that isolates long-seq heavy routes; run for 48h and report (ETA: 2029-04-14).
- Samira: add per-cohort TTL flagging and instrument staleness score (PR draft linked). (ETA: 2029-04-18).
- Evan: triage flaky compact-kv-eviction test and add more deterministic seedings (JIRA: SRV-4221) (ETA: 2029-04-13).
- Aisha: write short experiment brief for kernel-coalesce change with recommendations and schedule an ops sync (ETA: 2029-04-13).

Meeting notes / Attendees (post-smoke huddle):
- Aisha P. (note taker), Miguel O., Samira K., Evan L., Riley M. (ops); quick 25-min sync to surface findings and agree on immediate next steps.

Quick checklist for tomorrow's handoff:
- Ensure experiment tags are present in traces (kernel-coalesce=true / kv-ttl=40).
- Upload replay traces to experiment bucket and mark the ones we used.
- Add smoke-tests to nightly pipeline with these flags for short-run validation.

Useful links and references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1892 (kernel coalesce change)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1895 (ttl-and-metrics-instrumentation)
- JIRA: SRV-4217 (experiment tracking)
- JIRA: SRV-4221 (compact-kv-eviction flaky test)

Notes to self (rough thoughts):
- If we see increased GPU saturation during peak windows with lowered TTL, add a traffic-aware TTL circuit breaker that reverts to 120s when node GPU utilization > 78%.
- Consider a light-weight single-request fast-path we tried as a prototype last year (notes in Confluence - link in PR) — might recover median while keeping P95 gains.

If anything looks off or you want raw logs/traces I pushed them to gs://staging-replays/2029-04-11-evening-smoke/ (will keep for 7d).

-- Aisha
